solutions.check: 30 entries, 60 crossings, 0 conflicts; answers matched to the grid by number, direction and length

clue.text: Grand native of Belgrade going about on horseback

indicators.note: the Belgrade native's word goes round the riding word, enclosing it

parts.note: a Serb comes from Serbia, whose capital is Belgrade
a rider is said to be 'up' when mounted

explanation.surface: A splendid Serbian rides round on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' for on horseback is a racing usage: the jockey up is the one riding. 'Going about' is the container signal, not travel.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adjectives of praise, meaning magnificent or excellent.

clue.text: Second husband in unheated train

indicators.note: the husband's letter sits inside the unheated word

parts.note: something unheated is cool

explanation.surface: A second husband travelling in an unheated railway carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts H inside COOL, after S. 'Train' looks like a railway noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to teach or drill them, the same as training.

clue.text: Mass anger about force's petty thieving

indicators.note: the mass and anger words together go round the force letter

parts.note: a pile is a large mass
F is the abbreviation for force in physics
rage is fierce anger

explanation.surface: Widespread fury about the police force's minor stealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts F into PILERAGE, after PIL. 'Force' suggests the police, but it is just F.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilferage is the stealing of small items, minor theft.

clue.text: A poet wrote it? Sounds like Frost

indicators.note: sounds like says the frost word is to be taken by how it is said

parts.note: rime is hoar frost

explanation.surface: Was this verse written by the poet Robert Frost?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds like' turns RIME, a word for frost, into its soundalike. Frost is also the name of the American poet, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge wrote The Rime of the Ancient Mariner, and poets write verse that chimes.

clue.text: Areas of land male team leader is concerned about

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: the worrying word goes round the team's first letter

parts.note: to care is to be concerned

indicators.note: the leader of the word team is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A man who captains a team frets over things.
explanation.definitionFit: A hectare is a metric unit of land area, ten thousand square metres.

clue.text: Political grandee's shrubs chap with spades planted below gallery

parts.note: elders are shrubs bearing elderberries
the Tate is the London art gallery
S is the card abbreviation for spades
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A senior politician's shrubs being planted by a man with spades beneath an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Planted below' places the chap-and-spades pair after the gallery, as in a down entry. The Tate is a group of London art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder statesman is a senior, respected politician whose counsel is still sought.

clue.text: She has a will to try a magician's artifices, we hear

parts.note: to try something is to test it

indicators.note: we hear means the word is taken by how it is said

parts.note: a magician's artifices are tricks

explanation.surface: A woman determined to try a conjuror's illusions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' turns TRICKS into soundalike TRIX. 'Has a will' looks like determination but means a legal will.
explanation.definitionFit: A testatrix is a woman who has made a legal will.

clue.text: Spiritual leader reversed ban bishop originally introduced

indicators.note: the banning word is written backwards

parts.note: to bar is to ban
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A religious leader overturned a ban that a bishop first brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversed' turns BAR into RAB; 'originally' takes I from 'introduced'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher and leader.

clue.text: Left high and dry like a length of rope?

definitions.meaning: abandoned without help, like a beached ship
a rope is made of twisted strands, so it is, playfully, made of strands

explanation.surface: A castaway left with nothing but some rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Being marooned or abandoned is one sense; the other jokingly treats the word as 'having strands'.

clue.text: Concealing scam, stole more rigid-sounding reptile

parts.note: a boa is a long feathery stole or scarf
a con is a swindle

indicators.note: sounding means the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: stricter means more rigid

explanation.surface: Someone hiding a swindle stole a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounding' turns STRICTER into soundalike STRICTOR. 'Stole' looks like a verb but is the scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: The boa constrictor is a large South American snake, a reptile.

clue.text: Buddy used to broadcast, film here?

parts.note: Buddy Holly, the American rock-and-roll singer

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: 'would' expresses habit, as in 'he would sing every night'

explanation.surface: Buddy Holly once made radio broadcasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' signals that WOULD is said aloud, sounding like WOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Los Angeles district is the centre of the American movie industry, a place where films get made.

clue.text: Sedate person who weeps when a book has been withdrawn

indicators.note: the book's letter is taken away from the weeper's word

parts.note: one who sobs is a sobber
B is an abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A calm person who cries once a book is taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has been withdrawn' removes one B from SOBBER.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone serious, calm and restrained in manner.

clue.text: Source of metal in western half of a Pacific state

indicators.note: on the map the western half is the left-hand half, so the last three letters of the state's name go

parts.note: Oregon is a US state on the Pacific coast

explanation.surface: Mineral deposits in the western part of a Pacific coast state.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across entry, west is the left: 'western half of' keeps the first three of OREGON's six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ore is rock mined so that its metal can be extracted.

clue.text: Carpeting English cox in a riot, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests one possible arrangement of the letters, so they are reshuffled

explanation.surface: An English rowing cox caught up in a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals an anagram of COX IN A RIOT, giving XCORIATION. 'Carpeting' is a British word for a severe telling-off, not floor covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpeting is a stern rebuke, and an excoriation is a scathing denunciation.

clue.text: Caution about entering network of tunnels

indicators.note: the short word goes inside the cautioning word

parts.note: to caution someone is to warn them
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A warning about going into a tunnel system.
explanation.definitionFit: A warren is the system of burrows dug by rabbits.

clue.text: Quoting traveller, scoffing

parts.note: a rep, a sales representative, is a commercial traveller
to scoff is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: A salesman quoting prices while gobbling food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffing' is British slang for eating greedily, not mocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeating words said by another is quoting them.

clue.text: White ant? Call it white, ultimately

parts.note: to call something by a name is to term it

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A puzzled question whether a white ant should be called white.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' takes E, the last letter of 'white'. The question mark flags that this insect is not a true ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Termites are pale wood-eating insects popularly called white ants, though not related to ants.

clue.text: One girl embracing another? It's not real

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so one name goes within the other

parts.note: Mary is a girl's name
Gina is another girl's name

explanation.surface: One girl hugging another — or is it make-believe?
explanation.definitionFit: Something imaginary exists only in the mind, so it is not real.

clue.text: Rear of mansion as built ineptly outside port

indicators.note: the reworked letters go outside the mansion's last letter
ineptly means clumsily done, so the letters are rearranged
the rear of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: The back of a grand house was poorly built beyond the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ineptly' rearranges AS BUILT, and 'outside' wraps that round N, the rear of 'mansion'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Turkish city on the Bosphorus is a major seaport.

clue.text: Vessel bringing back leading Tory moderates?

indicators.note: bringing back means the combined words are read in reverse

parts.note: top means leading or foremost
wets was the Thatcher-era name for moderate Conservatives

explanation.surface: A pot that restores the leading moderate Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bringing back' reverses TOPWETS. Wets were the moderate Tories Margaret Thatcher disparaged in 1980s Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A stewpot is a cooking vessel in which stew is made.

clue.text: Revenue officer demanding head of this American feller

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a feller fells trees, and the American spelling of axeman drops the E

explanation.surface: A tax collector demanding the head of an American lumberjack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of' takes T from 'this'. 'Feller' is one who fells, an axeman, spelt AXMAN in American English.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxman is a collector of revenue for the state.

clue.text: Make beloved be aware of Cockney, following close

indicators.note: following means the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: the close of something is its end

indicators.note: Cockneys drop their aitches, so the H goes

parts.note: to hear of something is to be aware of it

explanation.surface: Win affection by being alert to Cockney speech, coming close behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class East Londoners, drop their aitches, so 'Cockney' removes the H. 'Close' is the noun meaning finish, not near.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear someone is to make them loved or liked.

clue.text: Expanse of water in Asia? A direct misrepresentation

indicators.note: a misrepresentation presents things wrongly, so the letters are presented in a new order

explanation.surface: A question whether a sea lies in Asia, met with a flat denial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misrepresentation' rearranges ASIA A DIRECT. The question mark is fair: this sea lies between Italy and the Balkans, not in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adriatic is an arm of the Mediterranean, a large expanse of sea water.

clue.text: An upright type like Popilius Lena?

definitions.meaning: the ordinary upright typeface, as opposed to italic
Popilius Laenas was a consul of ancient Rome

explanation.surface: Was a famous ancient consul an honest, upstanding fellow?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright type' seems to describe an honest person but is the plain upright typeface.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman type is the upright font; Popilius Laenas was a citizen of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Valuable quality bringing profit to strippers?

definitions.meaning: something that earns money, which for a stripper is a fine physique on show

explanation.surface: A useful trait that earns striptease artists their money.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a valued quality, and also anything that brings in income.

clue.text: Trendy new place to eat, drink and sleep

definitions.text: place to eat, drink and sleep

parts.note: in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A fashionable new venue for food, drink and a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a pub offering meals, drinks and lodging for travellers.

clue.text: Deer graduate bagged at first in Michigan

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

indicators.note: the bagged letter is put inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: MI is the postal abbreviation for Michigan

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A deer shot by a graduate, initially, in Michigan hunting country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' takes the opening letter of 'bagged'; 'in' places it within the state abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambi is the young deer of the Disney film, an example of a deer.

clue.text: Change coaches, one having left behind schedule

indicators.note: the numeral departs from the coaching word

parts.note: to coach is to train, so coaches means trains
I is the Roman numeral one
late means behind time

explanation.surface: A rail traveller swapping coaches after one has departed behind time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having left' removes I from TRAINS, giving TRANS. 'Coaches' looks like railway carriages but works as the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To translate is to change words into another language, or more broadly to convert.

clue.text: Wartime farm worker left with rejected equipment by lake

parts.note: and means together with

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a rig is a set of equipment

explanation.surface: Someone who left with discarded gear beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' reverses RIG to GIR. In Britain the Women's Land Army recruited land girls to work farms in both world wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Land girls were women drafted to work on farms during the two world wars.

clue.text: Celeb entertaining the old: one with enduring qualities

indicators.note: entertaining means holding inside, so the old word goes within the celebrity

parts.note: a celebrity is a star
ye is an old form of the, as in Ye Olde Shoppe

explanation.surface: A famous figure entertaining elderly people: someone of lasting appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old' looks like old people but means the archaic spelling of 'the', as in Ye Olde Shoppe; 'entertaining' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stayer is a horse or person with stamina, able to last a long distance.
